title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood of Austin, Texas, while in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The system did not slow down or stop before impact. This is a failure of object detection or response: the vehicle's perception system either did not identify the duck as an obstacle, or the decision system did not determine that stopping was necessary.

A human safety operator was in the vehicle but did not intervene to prevent the collision. It is not established whether the operator could have prevented the outcome, or what training and monitoring procedures were in place to enable intervention. The incident shows a gap between the presence of human oversight and its effectiveness in catching failures in real time.

Following the incident, Avride excluded certain streets from autonomous testing routes and began simulations to improve its systems. Whether these measures address the core failure—detection of small animals or pedestrians in the vehicle's path—is not established in the reporting.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which was in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck was well-known to residents because it had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant. Local residents discovered the duck's eggs and have placed them in an incubator for safekeeping.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating autonomously and stated that it found no evidence supporting a resident's claim that the car failed to stop at a stop sign. The company has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its autonomous vehicle routes. Avride is conducting simulations and controlled experiments to improve its technology and prevent similar situations in the future, while ensuring these changes do not compromise vehicle safety in other scenarios. Multiple autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, operate in Austin.
